docs.title: Asgard
docs.text:
"Loki collects the tricks.Thor of Asgard runs them." Key Features
  • Tasks in plain Ruby: a task is a method in a .loki file; every Thor DSL word (desc, method_option, long_desc, map, subcommand) works as written
  • Dependencies: depends_on runs prerequisites first, in sequence or in parallel stages, each at most once per run
  • Shell commands: execute shell scripts through user-defined shell environments, as foreground or background processes
  • Variables and helpers: @@name values shared by every task, helper methods usable in help text and task bodies alike
  • Subcommands: group tasks as asgard db migrate or asgard server start
  • Environment: dotenv loads a .env file; env(:port, "3000") reads a variable with a default
  • Auto-discovery: run asgard from any subdirectory; it finds the project's .loki by walking up
  • Multi-file projects: split tasks across *.loki files and pull them in with import
  • Scheduled tasks: schedule :backup, at: "02:00" and asgard schedule install hand a task to launchd or systemd
  • Watched files: watch :test, paths: "lib" and asgard watcher start run a task whenever files change
  • Background jobs: sh "mkdocs serve", background: true starts a job that outlives asgard; asgard jobs lists, stops and restarts it
  • Built-in flags: --version, --debug, --verbose and --doctor, which diagnoses a project's task files

Asgard is a command-line task runner for any project. You describe the tasks a project needs (build it, test it, deploy it, serve its docs) as short Ruby methods in a file named .loki, and asgard <task> runs them. Asgard orders prerequisites for you, runs independent ones in parallel, and can keep running tasks when you are not at the keyboard: on a timer, when files change, or as a background process you manage later.

The name is a small joke: Thor is the command-line toolkit asgard is built on, Asgard is where the tasks live, and Loki, the .loki file, holds all the tricks.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Install the command
gem install asgard

# Mark your project root
cd ~/work/myproject
touch .loki

# Add a first task
cat >> .loki << 'EOF'
class Tasks
  desc "Say hello"
  def hello = puts "Hello from Asgard!"
end
EOF

# Run it
asgard hello

Hello from Asgard!

asgard help lists every task the project defines, and asgard help hello shows the help for one of them.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
When you type asgard build, asgard looks for a file named .loki in the current directory, then in its parent, and so on up to the root of the filesystem. The first one it finds marks the project root, so the command works from any subdirectory of the project.

That .loki file is plain Ruby. Asgard has already defined a class named Tasks; your file reopens it and adds methods. Each public method with a desc is a task you can run from the command line:

class Tasks
  desc "Compile the project"
  def build = sh "rake build"

  depends_on :build
  desc "Run the tests"
  def test = sh "rake test"
end

Only .loki loads on its own. When a project outgrows one file, .loki says what else to load with import "*.loki", and every imported file reopens the same Tasks class.

Asgard is built on Thor, so the words you may know from other Ruby command-line tools work unchanged inside a .loki: desc, method_option, class_option, long_desc, argument, default_task, map and subcommand. Asgard adds its own on top: depends_on, sh and shebang (with background: for jobs), shell, default_shell, helper, header, footer, dotenv, schedule and watch.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Ruby 3.2 or later.
  • macOS or Linux for scheduled tasks and the file watcher (launchd on macOS, systemd user timers on Linux). Everything else works wherever Ruby does.
  • A C++17 compiler at install time: gem install asgard compiles one native extension. Xcode's command-line tools or a distribution's build-essential package is enough.

Asgard is on RubyGems; the source and issue tracker are on GitHub.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• sh is shebang — sh took only a script and forwarded it to shebang, so sh :python3, "..." was an ArgumentError while shebang :python3, "..." worked. sh is now alias_method :sh, :shebang: one method under two names, with the same arguments, keywords and behaviour. Nothing that worked before changes.
  • --debug and --verbose show one spelling in help — the two built-in boolean flags were listed as [--debug], [--no-debug], [--skip-debug] and the same for --verbose, the way Thor shows every boolean option. Negating a flag that defaults to off means nothing, so both now use no_negate, as --version and --doctor already did, and help lists just [--debug] and [--verbose]. The negated spellings still parse if typed.
  • BREAKING: project slugs carry a hash of the path — schedule labels, systemd unit names and the watcher's state directory were filed under the basename of the project directory alone, so two projects in directories of the same name shared them: schedule install in one removed the other's jobs, and their watchers fought over one pidfile. The slug is now the basename plus the CRC32 of the real path in hex, api-9f3a1c2b. Nothing migrates. Entries installed by an earlier version stay under the old slug, keep running, and show up in schedule list --all and watcher list --all as another project. Run asgard schedule remove and asgard watcher stop in each project before upgrading, then reinstall and restart afterwards. A leftover schedule entry can still be stopped as oldslug/name; a leftover watcher is stopped with kill $(cat ~/.local/state/asgard/watch/<old slug>/watcher.pid), and its state directory deleted. In project/name arguments the directory name alone now matches when it is unambiguous, and list --all flags a project whose directory no longer exists with [root missing]. The step-by-step guide is Upgrading to 0.6.0.
  • sh always runs bash — a one-line sh script used to go through /bin/sh (dash on Debian and Ubuntu) while a heredoc went through bash, so bash syntax failed or passed depending on line count. sh is now shebang :bash: one line or many is written to a tempfile and run by the :bash entry of the shells registry. Fixes #1.
  • BREAKING: exec: removed from sh and shebang — sh "cmd", exec: true replaced the asgard process with the command through Kernel.exec. Since sh is shebang :bash and every script runs as a file under its shell, the keyword no longer did what it promised: bash stayed as the parent and the command ran as its child, so a kill of the pid stopped bash and orphaned the command. The shell is the unit of work: the script ends, the shell ends, and Ctrl-C reaches asgard, the shell and the command together. Passing exec: now raises ArgumentError (unknown keyword: :exec); delete it from the call. See Upgrading to 0.6.0.
  • shebang is the one engine — every non-Ruby script takes the same path through Kernel#system; sh is shebang with the default shell.

  • A missing interpreter is reported — shebang :lua with no lua on PATH prints asgard: shell :lua not found: lua ... and exits 127 instead of exiting 127 silently.

  • A public method without a desc is a hidden task — it used to be no task at all: Thor printed a warning, asgard name was an unknown command, depends_on :name was an undefined task, and a depends_on written above it silently attached to the next task that had a desc. It is now a hidden task: it runs from the command line and as a dependency, help leaves it out, and --doctor lists it as hidden. depends_on always attaches to the very next method. A .loki that used public defs as helper methods now exposes them as runnable hidden tasks; make them private, put them in no_commands, or use helper.

  • Parallel dependencies each run on their own instance — tasks in one depends_on [:a, :b] stage used to share one Thor instance and could race on an instance variable. An instance variable set by a parallel dependency is therefore no longer visible to the task that depends on it (sequential dependencies still share it); pass values with dep_result.
  • A .loki that fails to load says so in one line — a missing import, a bad shell path, a syntax error or a typo used to print a Ruby backtrace. Now: asgard: /proj/.loki:2: undefined method 'dependz_on' for class Tasks (NoMethodError), exit 1. Set ASGARD_TRACE=1 for the backtrace.
  • --version and --doctor belong to asgard only before the task name — after it they are the task's own arguments.
  • Background job state is private — per-project state directories are created 0700 and schedule job files 0600, since logs, scripts and env: values can hold secrets.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Background jobs: sh ..., background: and asgard jobs — sh "mkdocs serve", background: true starts the script as a job that outlives asgard: a new session under a /bin/sh trampoline that records the exit status, stdin from /dev/null, stdout and stderr appended to a log. true names the job after the calling task and a per-run counter (doc_server-1, servers-2); a Symbol or String names it outright (background: :api) and takes no number. The call echoes the script, prints started <name> (pid N), log: <path> and returns a Jobs::Job (name, task, pid, log) at once; a job of that name already running is returned instead of started. shebang takes the same keyword, so a job may run under any registered shell. asgard jobs list shows each job as running, exited N (duration) or gone (--all across projects); stop [NAME...] resolves job names, task names and the depends_on closure, sends TERM to each job's process group newest first and KILL after --timeout (default 10s); log NAME [-f] prints or follows the log; restart NAME stops the job and runs its task again; clean forgets every job that is not running. Records live under $XDG_STATE_HOME/asgard/jobs/<slug>/ and a pid is trusted only while its command line still carries the job's script, so a pid reused after a reboot shows as gone. A trailing & in a script is still the shell's detached mode: asgard reports success and keeps no record. Asgard::Pid and Asgard::StateDir are lifted out of the watcher and shared; Schedule::Table takes headers:, keys: and flexible: and hands tty-table exact content widths, which also stops it squeezing a one-row table. csh and tcsh scripts get .csh.
  • shells registry and shell DSL — Tasks.shells maps a name to { path:, args:, ext: }, seeded with :bash, :sh, :python3, :python, :node, :ruby and :perl. shell :strict, "bash -eu -o pipefail" registers a shell: the path string is Shellwords-split, its first word is the executable and the rest precede args: (a String or an Array); ext: defaults by the executable's basename. Pin a path with shell :bash, "/opt/homebrew/bin/bash" so scheduled and watched tasks, whose PATH lacks Homebrew, run the same bash as the terminal. A Pathname path is the executable whole, never split, so a directory with a space in it needs no quoting. The name may be left out: shell "/usr/local/bin/bash -c -w" registers :bash, named after the executable, with the options parsed into args, and shell :zsh alone registers zsh from PATH. shell returns the name. The executable is checked as the .loki loads: a path with a directory part must be an executable file, a bare name must be on PATH, else ArgumentError naming the shell, rather than an exit 127 the first time a task runs. An unregistered name still runs as itself from PATH with .tmp.

  • default_shell — default_shell :strict at class level picks the registry entry that sh, and shebang called with a script alone, run; it starts as :bash and reads back with no argument. A bare Symbol only selects and never changes the registry. Every other form registers through shell first, then selects: default_shell "/usr/local/bin/bash -c -w" pins and picks :bash in one line, default_shell :strict, "bash", args: "-eu -o pipefail" declares and selects :strict, and the path is the name when only args: or ext: are given. sh and shebang return true on success.

  • asgard schedule remove [NAME] and asgard schedule prune [--dry-run] — remove one entry (project/name reaches another project's), or every project's entries whose project directory is gone.

  • Watcher triggers that wait for a busy task merge — three saves during a long run now queue one more run with every change, not three.
  • Watcher log rotation — watcher.log moves to watcher.log.1 once it passes 10 MB (ASGARD_LOG_MAX bytes to change it).
  • CI — .github/workflows/test.yml runs the suite on Linux and macOS, Ruby 3.4 and 4.0.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• import_up from an imported file no longer recurses — the root .loki is loaded directly, not through import, so it was never recorded as loaded; a child file's import_up found it, reloaded it, and the two imported each other until the stack overflowed. asgard --doctor died the same way. The root is now recorded before it loads.
  • A child ended by a signal no longer crashes sh — exit was given the nil exit status of a signalled process and raised a TypeError. sh and shebang now exit with 128 plus the signal number, as a shell would, through Asgard::Shell.exit_code, which the watcher's worker shares.
  • A failing parallel dependency waits for its siblings — the first failure in a depends_on [:a, :b] group used to end the process at once, leaving the other tasks' subprocesses running detached. Every thread in the group is now joined first. When more than one fails, each is named on stderr (asgard: dependency 'lint' failed: exit 1) and the error lists them.
  • A raising parallel dependency no longer prints Ruby's thread report — the full "terminated with exception" backtrace preceded asgard's own message. Dependency threads now run with report_on_exception off; the error still reaches the top level and is reported once.
  • Task and helper names Thor relies on are rejected at load time — a task named args broke every command with an arity error pointing at Thor, and names on Thor's own reserved list (shell, options, invoke, ...) raised a bare RuntimeError. Defining any of them, as a task or inside no_commands, now raises Asgard::Error with the file and line, which asgard --doctor reports as a load failure.
  • The gem's own doc_tasks.loki ran without direnv — it built paths from ENV['RR'], which only the repository's .envrc sets, so a fresh clone crashed on asgard help. It now finds the root through loki_up.

  • The watcher no longer trusts a pid it cannot identify — a pidfile left by a crash or a reboot can name a pid that an unrelated process now holds; list called it running, start refused, and stop sent TERM to it. The daemon's pid, and each entry's, must now belong to an asgard process with the expected command line (watcher run, or the task's name), read through ps. A stale pidfile is simply not running, and start replaces it.

  • A task waiting on a shared dependency that failed no longer runs — with top depending on [b, c] and both on a, a failing a let c run anyway. It now stops, and asgard ends with a's own exit status.

  • asgard jobs stop can no longer signal asgard's own process group — a stale record whose pid had become asgard's own (pid reuse after a reboot) verified as the job, and the group TERM and KILL reached asgard and its pipeline.
  • The watcher reloads on a .loki change — the reload stopped its own listener from the listener's thread, which Listen refuses, so the daemon kept running but watched nothing. It now re-execs from the main thread once running tasks finish, keeps its lock across the exec, and keeps the running declarations when the edited task files do not load.
  • A failed spawn no longer kills a watcher worker — E2BIG (a huge change list), a missing root or executable now report exit 127/126 and the next trigger still runs. Change lists over 128 KB travel in a file named by ASGARD_CHANGES_FILE, which changes reads. A full queue drops the trigger instead of stalling every other watch.
  • Watcher shutdown waits for a trigger being routed, and leaves no task running unrecorded; tasks and the daemon get /dev/null as stdin; an idle daemon no longer spins (about 6% of a core before); two watcher starts at once can no longer leave two daemons (watcher.lock); signal traps are set before Listen starts; a failed start cleans up; list shows "did not finish" for a task that died without an exit; plain paths are judged in the project root and a dotted directory is a directory; globs inside {} work; GEM_, RUBYOPT, RUBYLIB and BUNDLE(R)_ reach tasks; a report that cannot be written no longer ends the reporter; only loaded and root-level .loki files trigger a reload; a task name matches only as a whole word.
  • Background jobs: concurrent starts of one name start one job; a start returns only once the job runs its trampoline (an immediate second start used to miss it under load); TERM is re-sent during the grace period; ps -ww keeps long command lines whole on Linux; a failed exec reports and exits 127; close_others; a task named ready? gets a listable job; a job whose trampoline alone died is still verified and stoppable; stop --all NAME is refused; bare asgard jobs works outside a project; a task that changes directory still files its jobs under its project; the log help text says the log holds the latest run.
  • Schedules: a $ in a systemd env: value stays one $; on: [] and at: [] are rejected; "weekends" reads back as weekends; a dashed task name schedules its underscored command and a : gets a clear message; newlines and other control characters in options and env, and env names that are not identifiers, are rejected; an unchanged launchd install leaves a running job alone; a plist that fails plutil never replaces the installed one; a failed first systemd install is not taken for a stop; launchd status reports running jobs and signal exits.
  • Core: a .loki directory is not a task file; an unregistered zsh or fish keeps its script extension, and default_shell :name checks that the shell exists; Tasks.subclasses is Ruby's again; a corrupt state record no longer crashes a listing; the gem's release prompt survives stdin at end of input.
  • Packaging: the gem ships only lib/, bin/asgard, sig/ and the README, LICENSE and CHANGELOG; the description and changelog link are corrected.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Watched files, built in — watch :task, paths: "lib/**/*.rb" at class level in a .loki declares that a task runs when matching files change, with only:, ignore:, events:, debounce:, env: and as: keywords. asgard watcher start|stop|list|preview|log|run manages the watcher: one background process per project that runs each trigger as asgard <task> from the project root, with a fixed environment (a whitelist of the daemon's variables, the entry's env:, .envrc through direnv exec) plus the changed paths in ASGARD_MODIFIED, ASGARD_ADDED and ASGARD_REMOVED. Different tasks run concurrently; the same task never overlaps itself, and a trigger that arrives while its task runs is queued behind it. Saving a .loki file restarts the watcher with the new declarations. stop lets a running task finish. list shows each entry's last run; --all covers every project. State and logs live under ~/.local/state/asgard/watch/. The command is registered as the gem-owned _watcher and mapped to watcher. The daemon and every trigger run the same asgard executable that started the watcher, by absolute path, even under direnv exec. See Watched Files.
  • changes Kernel method — inside a task, the Asgard::Changes the watcher triggered it with (modified, added, removed, all, empty?); every list is empty when the task is run by hand.
  • Asgard::Watch::Error (subclass of Asgard::Error) — raised when a watch names a task the project does not define.
  • examples/do.loki — asgard do lint test build runs tasks in sequence, with comma-separated steps for arguments and options (asgard do hello Alice, farewell Bob --formal). A plain user task, not a built-in; it stops at the first failure.
  • examples/confirm.loki — a hidden confirm task to list first in a dangerous task's depends_on; answering anything but y/yes aborts with exit 1. Refuses without a terminal unless ASGARD_YES is set.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• New runtime dependencies: listen (file events) and ractor_queue (the queue between the daemon and its worker Ractors). ractor_queue is a native extension, so gem install asgard now compiles and needs a C++17 compiler; Asgard was pure Ruby before.
  • Asgard::Schedule::Table.draw takes headers: so watcher list can reuse it; a running state renders green.
  • Asgard.machine_wide? is true for watcher list as well as schedule list, so both work from a directory with no .loki above it.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Usage errors exit 1 — a missing argument, an unknown command, or a bad subcommand (asgard greet with no NAME, asgard nope) printed Thor's error but exited 0, so CI and scripts saw success. Asgard::Base now defines exit_on_failure? as true.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• asgard schedule list --all (-a) — lists every project's scheduled entries, one table per project under a Project: name (/full/path/to/project) header. Other projects' .loki files are not loaded: their COMMAND and SCHEDULE columns, and the project path, are read back from the installed launchd plist or systemd unit files. Outside any .loki tree, asgard schedule list shows every project automatically instead of failing with "no .loki file found".
  • stop, start, trigger and log accept entries of other projects, so they work from any directory. A bare name matches this project's entry first, then any other project's; when two other projects share a name, write it as project/name.
  • A project-scoped list with nothing installed now ends with "Use asgard schedule list --all to see all currently scheduled tasks."
  • Backend API: installed_entries (every project's entries), installed_columns(name) and installed_directory(name) (read from the job files) on both the launchd and systemd backends.
  • Runtime dependency: tty-table (~> 0.12), which brings pastel and tty-screen.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• asgard schedule list prints a table — NAME, COMMAND, SCHEDULE, STATE and LAST EXIT, with long cells wrapped to the terminal width, replacing one text line per entry. A run of hourly times collapses (10:00-17:00 hourly weekdays). Color is used on a terminal and turned off by NO_COLOR or when piped.
  • The not-installed messages from stop, start, trigger and log point at asgard schedule list --all.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Scheduled entries were invisible outside the directory tree of the project that installed them: list and every per-entry command were scoped to the project found from the current directory, so launchctl list showed jobs that asgard schedule list did not.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Scheduled tasks, built in — schedule :task, at: "17:30", on: :weekdays (or every: 3600) at class level in a .loki declares a periodic run, and asgard schedule preview|install|list|start|stop|trigger|log|remove manages the entries under launchd (macOS) or systemd user timers (Linux). Missed calendar runs fire on wake; a project .envrc is loaded at run time through direnv exec. Promoted from the standalone dev/schedule.loki; job labels and paths are unchanged, so entries it installed are still recognized. ActiveSupport is no longer required: every: takes seconds or any object with in_seconds. The command is registered as the gem-owned _schedule and mapped to schedule. See Scheduled Tasks.
  • Asgard::Schedule::Error (subclass of Asgard::Error) — raised when launchctl/systemctl fails; Asgard.run! reports it as a one-line asgard: ... message.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Upgrading from dev/schedule.loki: remove import_up "dev/schedule.loki" from your .loki. Its Tasks.schedule overrides the built-in one and records declarations where asgard schedule never looks.
  • Asgard::Error and Asgard::CircularDependencyError now live in lib/asgard/errors.rb, loaded first. No change to the classes themselves.
  • The gem's own test run (test_check, test_verbose) loads every test/test_*.rb in one process, so coverage is measured across the whole suite.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • asgard <task> now exits 1 when the task returns :fail — quality-gate tasks (*_check) signal failure by returning :fail; previously that result was discarded and asgard always exited 0, so callers relying on the exit status (CI, cross-repo runners like ws_quality.loki) saw every individual gate as passing. The aggregate quality task was unaffected (it aborts itself). Only a top-level result of exactly :fail maps to exit 1; :warn and :skip remain non-blocking.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• helper(name, &block) DSL method on Asgard::Base — defines a method available in both class context (e.g. inside header or footer) and as a private instance method inside task bodies, with a single declaration. Eliminates the manual def self.name + no_commands { private def name = self.class.name } boilerplate. Supports positional arguments, keyword arguments, default values, and block arguments. 

    class Tasks
  @@project ||= "myapp".freeze

  helper(:version) {
    File.read("lib/myapp/version.rb").match(/VERSION\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"/)[1].freeze
  }

  header "#{@@project} v#{version}"   # class context

  desc "Show the current version"
  def show_version = puts version     # instance context
end

  • header(text) and footer(text) DSL methods on Asgard::Base — attach static text to the general help output. header lines are printed above the commands list; footer lines are printed below the options block. Multiple calls accumulate: each header call appends a line, each footer call prepends a line, so content from later-loaded files naturally wraps around content from earlier files. Neither appears when asgard help <command> is called for per-command detail. 

    class Tasks
  header "my-project — build & release tasks"
  footer "See https://example.com/docs for details"
end

  • no_negate(*names) DSL method on Asgard::Base — suppresses the [--no-name] and [--skip-name] negation variants from help output for boolean class options where negation is meaningless. Call it after the class_option declaration: 
    class_option :version, type: :boolean, default: false, desc: "Show version and exit"
no_negate :version

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• --version reimplemented as a class_option — the flag now appears in the "Options" section of asgard help alongside --debug and --verbose, rather than as a listed command. The _version method and its map "--version" => :_version registration have been removed. The actual early-exit behaviour still lives in Asgard.run! (before the .loki file is required), so --version works even when no .loki file exists. no_negate :version suppresses the spurious [--no-version] / [--skip-version] variants.
  • loki_up returns Pathname instead of String — the return value is now a Pathname instance (or nil when not found). Pathname is accepted everywhere loki_up's result is used: import, dotenv, load, and standard Ruby file methods all accept Pathname via to_path / to_s. Code that passes the result directly to those methods is unaffected; code that performs string operations on the path should call .to_s first.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Help output showed tasks prefix before every command — asgard help displayed asgard tasks build instead of asgard build. The cause was a keyword-vs-positional mismatch in the Asgard::Base#help override: declaring subcommand: false as a keyword argument caused Ruby's super to forward it as the hash {subcommand: false}. Thor's banner method received this hash as the positional subcommand argument, treated it as truthy, and prepended the class namespace (tasks) to every command name. Fixed by changing the override signature to match Thor's positional signature: def help(command = nil, subcommand = false).

docs.title: Added (continued)
docs.text:
• loki_up(name = ".loki") Kernel method — searches Dir.pwd and each ancestor directory for a file with the given name; returns the absolute path of the first match or nil. Available everywhere in Ruby (task bodies, .loki files, top-level code) as a module_function on Kernel.
  • import(path) Kernel method — loads a .loki file (or a glob of .loki files) with require-like idempotency via $LOADED_FEATURES. Accepts a String or Pathname. Relative paths are resolved relative to the caller's file (like require_relative). Glob patterns (*.loki, **/*.loki) expand via Dir.glob and load all matches. Returns true if any file was newly loaded, false if all were already loaded or no glob matches were found. Raises ArgumentError if the path does not end with .loki.
  • import_up(name = ".loki") Kernel method — combines loki_up and import. For exact names, finds the first ancestor directory containing that file and loads it. For glob names, finds the first ancestor directory containing any matching files and loads them all — stopping at that level rather than aggregating across multiple ancestors. Returns false if nothing is found.
  • debug? and verbose? Kernel module functions — thin wrappers around $DEBUG and $VERBOSE, available everywhere in Ruby as module_function on Kernel. Set via --debug / --verbose CLI flags or directly via $DEBUG / $VERBOSE.
  • env(name, default = nil) Kernel method — fetches a system environment variable by symbol or string name, upcasing the key automatically. env(:port, "3000") returns "3000" when PORT is unset; env(:api_key) raises KeyError when API_KEY is missing and no default is provided. Accepts both env(:port) and env("PORT") forms. Cleaner than ENV['PORT'] in task bodies.
  • Verbose/debug feedback for import and import_up — when verbose? is true, each file loaded is printed to stderr. When debug? is true, already-loaded files are also reported (with an "already loaded" suffix), and import_up reports when a file is not found.
  • RuboCop lint gate — RuboCop is now a first-class quality gate alongside tests and Flog. Added rubocop to the Gemfile, a .rubocop.yml tuned for this codebase (Ruby 3.2 target, relaxed Metrics thresholds consistent with Flog as the primary complexity gate, examples/ excluded), and rake rubocop / rake rubocop_fix tasks backed by a tmp/rubocop_cache directory for fast re-runs.
  • Expanded rake quality task — quality now runs three independent gates (tests + coverage, RuboCop, Flog) in parallel using depends_on [:test, :rubocop, :flog_check]. Each gate captures its pass/fail result in an instance variable; output is suppressed on pass and filtered to failures only on fail, preventing interleaved output from concurrent subprocesses. A formatted pass/fail summary table is printed after all gates complete, so every failure is visible in a single run.
  • rake flog_check task — replaces the bare flog lib/ call with a structured task that enforces per-method thresholds (warn ≥20, fail ≥50), lists warnings and failures in separate sections, and exits non-zero only when the failure threshold is breached.
  • Single-argument desc shorthand — desc now accepts one string (the description) with the usage string omitted. The usage defaults to the method name, eliminating the redundant first argument for the common case: 
    desc "Run the test suite"   # usage defaults to "test"
def test = sh "bundle exec rake test"
    The two-argument form (desc "usage", "description") still works unchanged and is still required when the usage string differs from the method name (e.g. desc "build NAME", "Build an artifact").
  • default_task override warning — Asgard::Base now overrides Thor's default_task to warn to stderr when a second call would silently replace the first. The warning includes the task name, file, and line number for both the original declaration and the override, making accidental cross-file clobbering visible immediately.
  • examples/env_usage.loki and examples/.env — demonstrate the env() Kernel helper, including the default-fallback form (env(:log_level, "info")) for variables absent from the environment. Uses loki_up(".env") so dotenv locates the .env file correctly regardless of which directory asgard is invoked from.
  • examples/subdir/ — three-file demo showing import and import_up across directory boundaries: subdir/.loki imports import_up_demo.loki by name; import_up_demo.loki calls import_up "env_usage.loki" to locate and load a file from an ancestor directory without a hardcoded path.
  • status task in kitchen_sink.loki — demonstrates debug? and verbose? predicates with conditional output; shows --debug printing $DEBUG, $VERBOSE, and the full options hash.
  • Computed value methods in kitchen_sink.loki — three private methods (version, sha, branch) demonstrating the idiomatic Ruby replacement for the removed var DSL, including memoization via @ivar ||=.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• var DSL method — removed in favour of native Ruby class variables. Use @@name ||= "value".freeze in the class body. Class variables are visible in all task instance methods and in subcommand subclasses, making them the correct tool for shared configuration in a Thor-based task runner. Breaking change for projects using var.
  • import DSL method — import(mod) was a one-line alias for Ruby's built-in include. Callers can use include directly.
  • --auto-load CLI flag — sibling *.loki loading is now entirely user-controlled: place import "*.loki" (or any glob or explicit path) at the top of your .loki file to load additional task files. Breaking change for projects that relied on --auto-load.
  • Asgard.load_loki(dir) — replaced by import with glob support. Callers can use import(File.join(dir, "*.loki")) directly.
  • debug? / verbose? private methods on Tasks — removed as redundant. The identical module_function versions on Kernel are available everywhere, including inside task bodies.

docs.title: Refactored
docs.text:
• validate_deps! decomposed into focused private helpers — the method was performing four unrelated validations in one body (orphaned depends_on check, undefined dep name check, dep arity check, cycle detection). Each concern is now a dedicated _-prefixed private method (_check_orphaned_deps!, _check_undefined_deps!, _check_dep_arities!, _build_and_sort_graph). validate_deps! is now a sequencer of ~8 lines. Flog score dropped from 87.3 to 24.4.
  • invoke_command dispatch helpers made private with descriptive names — the dispatch hook was decomposed into focused helpers. Those helpers (acquire_run_token, run_deps_for, run_dep_group, signal_done, run_dep) are now declared private on Asgard::Base rather than wrapped in no_commands. The _ prefix was dropped — the underscore convention is reserved for gem-owned methods on Tasks; private is sufficient to exclude instance methods from Thor's command registry. invoke_command itself stays in no_commands so Thor does not warn about an undescribed public method.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Multiple parallel dep failures now all surfaced — when two or more parallel deps raised, only the first exception was re-raised; the rest were silently discarded. All errors are now printed to stderr via warn before a general Asgard::Error is raised. When only one dep fails, its exception is re-raised directly as before.
  • Subcommand deps not validated at startup — run! only called Tasks.validate_deps!, so circular dependencies and undefined dep names in subcommand groups were silently ignored. run! now snapshots Asgard::Base.subclasses before loading task files and validates every newly defined subclass alongside Tasks.
  • Parallel dep thread orphaned on exception — when a parallel dep group contained one fast-failing task and one slow task, the join loop re-raised the first thread's exception and abandoned the remaining threads. The join loop now collects all thread exceptions before re-raising, ensuring every thread completes before execution exits the group.
  • Dep with required arguments gave a cryptic runtime error — depends_on :build where build(name) has required parameters caused Thor::InvocationError at task invocation time with no indication of where the problem was. validate_deps! now checks arity via instance_method.parameters and raises Asgard::Error at startup with the task name and argument count.
  • Orphaned depends_on silently discarded — a depends_on declaration at the end of a class body with no following desc/def left @_pending_deps non-empty but was ignored by validate_deps! due to an early return if _deps.empty? guard. validate_deps! now checks @_pending_deps before that guard and raises Asgard::Error naming the orphaned dependencies.
  • Single-arg desc options silently dropped — when desc "description", hide: true was used, Ruby routed the options hash to the description positional parameter. The override now detects a Hash in the description position and treats it as options.
  • Single-arg desc stolen by no_commands blocks — if a no_commands block appeared between a single-arg desc and its method, method_added consumed @_pending_single_desc for the interstitial helper and leaked a stale @usage onto the next real command. The fix: @_pending_single_desc is only consumed when no_commands? is false.
  • Parallel dep race condition — when two parallel tasks shared a common dependency, the second thread could start before the shared dep finished. _ran_tasks (a single Set) has been replaced with _running / _done Sets and a per-task ConditionVariable. Threads that arrive at an already-running dep now wait for its completion.
  • depends_on silently dropped before no_commands blocks — the method_added guard now checks @usage instead of the no_commands? counter, so no_commands helpers placed between depends_on and def no longer silently steal the dependency.
  • shebang ignored its silent: keyword argument — the parameter was accepted but never referenced; the script body is now echoed to stdout unless silent: true is passed, matching the behavior of sh.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• validate_deps! detects undefined dependency names — depends_on :nonexistent previously passed validation silently and produced no error at runtime. validate_deps! now raises Asgard::Error listing every dep name that does not correspond to a defined task.
  • default_task behaviour documented — docs/tasks.md now notes that running asgard with no arguments displays the help message when default_task is not set.
  • loki_up scope clarified in docs — docs/task-files.md and docs/api.md now make explicit that loki_up locates any file by name, not just .loki files, with examples for .env and VERSION. The dotenv loki_up(".env") || ".env" pattern is shown as the canonical way to load a .env file from any subdirectory.
  • examples/.loki — updated to use explicit import "*.loki" (sibling files) and import "subdir/import_demo.loki" (subdirectory file), with comments explaining import, import_up, and loki_up.

docs.title: Added (continued)
docs.text:
• --doctor built-in CLI flag — diagnoses .loki resolution, import chains, and task definitions for the current directory, then exits. Handled directly in Asgard.run! before the .loki file is loaded (same pattern as --version), so it keeps working in exactly the situations that would otherwise abort the whole process: a broken .loki file, a circular or undefined dependency, or a task silently redefined by a later def. Backed by the new Asgard::Doctor class. The report includes a "Tasks by file" listing: every command grouped by the file it's defined in, printed as relative/path:line so an editor can jump straight to it. A task name defined at more than one location gets every definition annotated inline — the earlier one(s) as OVERRIDDEN by <file>:<line> — never callable, the winning (last) one as active — redefines <file>:<line> — replacing the old flat "Tasks#x redefined" summary line with an annotation right where the problem is. See API Reference.
  • Flay and Reek quality gates — flay_check checks for structural code duplication (mass ≥ 150); reek checks code smells. Both run as part of quality alongside test, rubocop, and flog_check. A .reek.yml tunes several detectors to this codebase's conventions (no doc-comment requirement, short variable names, disabled TooManyStatements, etc), plus per-method exclude: entries (generated with reek --todo and hand-curated) that grandfather specific reviewed smells at specific methods — precise enough that a genuinely new smell still fails the gate even at an already-reviewed method, unlike a per-file count.
  • test_verbose task — runs the test suite with Minitest's verbose (-v) output.
  • Colorized quality gate summary — quality's final report now prints a green/red PASS/FAIL badge per gate plus a passed/failed tally, via a shared print_quality_summary helper.
  • console task — opens an IRB console with the gem loaded (bin/console if present, otherwise bundle exec irb).
  • git.loki — per-repo git tasks (push, pull, fetch), imported from .loki.

docs.title: Changed (continued)
docs.text: • release task now prompts for confirmation (Release asgard vX.Y.Z to RubyGems? [y/N]) unless -y/--yes is passed, before tagging and pushing.

docs.title: Fixed (continued)
docs.text: • bin/asgard could silently run the wrong asgard version — the executable did require "asgard", which (without bundle exec) is resolved by RubyGems independently of where the script itself lives, so it could load a separately-installed gem version instead of this repo's own lib/. Changed to require_relative "../lib/asgard" so the executable always loads the library that ships alongside it, regardless of what else is installed.

docs.title: Added (continued 2)
docs.text:
• SKIP and WARN quality-gate statuses — alongside PASS/FAIL. Both are non-blocking (quality only aborts on FAIL); SKIP is for a required external tool that isn't installed, WARN is for a check that ran successfully but has non-blocking suggestions. print_quality_summary renders all four with distinct colored badges and a combined tally.
  • typos_check / typos_fix tasks — spell-checking via the external typos CLI (brew install typos-cli, not a gem dependency). typos_check writes full findings to typos_output.txt and participates in quality. If typos isn't installed, the gate prints a one-line notice recommending brew install typos-cli and reports SKIP rather than failing.
  • fasterer_check task — runs the fasterer gem (new dev dependency) against lib/, reporting performance-idiom suggestions as WARN (non-blocking) — these are suggestions on working code, not correctness problems.
  • asgard tree now shows the project header/footer — Base#tree wraps Thor's built-in command tree the same way Base#help already wraps the command list, so both example outputs are consistent.
  • Every quality gate (test_check, rubocop_check, flog_check, flay_check, reek_check, typos_check, fasterer_check, bundler_audit_check) now writes its full detailed output to a <gate>_output.txt file at the repo root (gitignored via *_output.txt) and prints only a one-line summary to stdout — full detail stays on disk without cluttering the terminal.

docs.title: Changed (continued 2)
docs.text:
• Asgard::Base and Asgard::Doctor split into focused mixins — Asgard::Base (31 methods) is now Registry, DependencyGraph, TaskDSL, and Dispatch (lib/asgard/base/*.rb), with method_added/header/footer/help/tree remaining directly on the class as the orchestrator. Asgard::Doctor (19 methods) is now TaskSections and Report (lib/asgard/doctor/*.rb), with the diagnostic flow (run, report_markers, load_chain, etc.) staying on the class itself. Purely a file-organization change — behavior, asgard help/asgard --doctor output, and the public API are unchanged. Drops Reek's TooManyMethods/TooManyInstanceVariables warnings on both classes to zero.
  • Reek grandfathering made precise — replaced the per-file smell-count baseline (.quality/reek_baseline.txt, the reek_baseline task) with per-method, per-detector exclude: entries in .reek.yml itself, generated via reek --todo and hand-curated. Unlike a count, this still catches a genuinely new smell at an already-reviewed method, without relying on the file's total count staying the same. The reek_baseline and ensure_quality_dir tasks and the .quality/ directory have been removed as no longer needed.

docs.title: Added (continued 3)
docs.text:
• depends_on accepts a Proc/lambda in addition to a fixed list — a sole callable defers resolution to validate_deps! (once, right after every .loki file has loaded) instead of resolving immediately when depends_on itself is evaluated. This solves the "load order matters" problem for a dependency list that can't be known upfront — e.g. "every task whose name ends in _check," discovered across several files including ones imported conditionally (import "quality_rails.loki" if defined?(Rails)). The Proc must return the same shape the splat form would receive (an array of stages, each a Symbol or Array); it's written directly in the class body, so it lexically captures that class as self and can call all_commands bare. A Proc that raises is re-raised as Asgard::Error naming the task it was declared for; a Proc that resolves to an undefined task or a cycle is still caught by the existing startup validation, since the resolved result is checked exactly like a plain array. See Dynamic Dependencies.
  • bundler_audit_check task — runs bundle-audit check --update against Gemfile.lock (new dev dependency bundler-audit); reports FAIL on any known vulnerability, since this is a security gate, not a suggestion.
  • quality_rails.loki — imported by .loki only when Rails is defined; currently ships brakeman_check, a Rails security-scan example. Needs no wiring into quality's dependency list — quality's depends_on Proc discovers it automatically once it's loaded.

docs.title: Changed (continued 3)
docs.text: • test, rubocop, reek renamed to test_check, rubocop_check, reek_check — for consistency with the other gates, all of which already ended in _check. This convention is what makes automatic discovery possible: quality's depends_on Proc finds every task whose name matches _check\z rather than naming them one by one.

docs.title: Removed (continued)
docs.text: • dagwood runtime dependency — replaced by stdlib TSort for the one thing it was still doing (cycle detection); the parallel-execution plan itself was already derived directly from depends_on's stage list, not from a rebuilt DAG. _build_dep_graph (dead code — its return value was already unused) is deleted along with the gemspec entry.

docs.title: Changed (continued 4)
docs.text: • validate_deps! cycle detection now uses stdlib TSort instead of Dagwood::DependencyGraph#order — a private Graph Struct (edges member, include TSort) owns the task→dependency Hash and the traversal, raising TSort::Cyclic on a cycle exactly as before (converted to Asgard::CircularDependencyError). run_deps_for no longer round-trips through a rebuilt DAG on every dispatch — it iterates _deps[target]'s stage groups directly, which is already the parallel-execution plan depends_on built.

docs.title: Fixed (continued 2)
docs.text: • quality.loki's parallel *_check tasks raced on shared instance state — each *_check task wrote its pass/fail status to an ivar on self (@test_result, @rubocop_result, ...) from inside a Thread.new spawned by the same parallel-dependency group — an unsynchronized write across threads that MRI's GVL happens to hide today but would not on JRuby/TruffleRuby. Fixed at the framework level: Dispatch#run_dep_group now collects each task's own return value into a Hash (via Thread#value), run_deps_for merges per-stage results, and a new dep_result/dep_results instance API (backed by Thread.current, not self) hands them to the task body that depends on them. quality.loki and quality_rails.loki's *_check tasks now return their status as a plain value instead of writing to an ivar; quality reads dep_result(name) instead of instance_variable_get.

docs.title: Added (continued 4)
docs.text: • examples/bad.loki — a worked demonstration of the race the fix above addresses: 4 parallel workers read-modify-write a shared @hits counter directly (the anti-pattern quality.loki used to have), reliably losing updates. Kept as a contrast example for what dep_result/dep_results is for.

docs.title: Added (continued 5)
docs.text:
• sh(script, exec: true) — hands the command the asgard process itself via Kernel.exec instead of forking. For a task's final, long-running command (a dev server, a REPL) this replaces the ruby process outright, so nothing sits resident in memory behind it and Ctrl-C is handled directly by the command instead of unwinding back through asgard. doc_tasks.loki's doc_server task (sh "mkdocs serve", exec: true) is the motivating example. See Shell Helpers.
  • bootstrap and env_info tasks in kitchen_sink.loki — demonstrate sh with a multi-line heredoc (routed through bash -c) and a single-line command, respectively.

docs.title: Fixed (continued 3)
docs.text: • Ctrl-C during a running sh command printed a raw Interrupt backtrace — SIGINT hits the whole foreground process group, so asgard's own ruby process raised Interrupt independently of whatever the shelled-out command did with the signal, and it went uncaught, unwinding through Thor and printing a stack trace before exiting. Asgard.run! now rescues Interrupt and exits with the conventional 130 status.

docs.title: Added (continued 6)
docs.text:
• depends_on accepts a block in addition to a Proc/lambda — depends_on { ... } (or depends_on do ... end for a block spanning multiple statements) defers resolution to validate_deps! exactly like the existing sole-Proc/lambda form; the two are interchangeable. depends_on still accepts task arguments or a block, never both — combining them raises Asgard::Error. See Dynamic Dependencies.
  • The resolved Proc/lambda/block result is now shape-validated — once validate_deps! calls it, the return value must be an Array of stages, each a Symbol/String (sequential) or an Array of Symbol/String (parallel group), nested no deeper than that. A bad shape (wrong type, an invalid stage, a non-Symbol/String leaf, or nesting more than one level deep) now raises Asgard::Error naming the task and the offending value, instead of failing later with an opaque NoMethodError.
  • examples/depends_on_block/good/ and examples/depends_on_block/bad/ — two self-contained example projects (each its own .loki root, isolated from the main examples/ tree) demonstrating the block form: good/ covers single-line { ... }, do...end, and a mixed sequential+parallel shape; bad/ demonstrates the double-wrapped-array mistake that the new shape validation catches, with the exact Asgard::Error message it produces.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• *.loki files are no longer auto-loaded by default. Pass --auto-load to asgard to load all *.loki files from the project root alphabetically before .loki. This is a breaking change for projects using the multi-file layout.
  • Added --auto-load as a built-in CLI flag in Tasks, visible in asgard help

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• --version built-in CLI flag — prints Asgard::VERSION and exits; implemented as a _-prefixed method in Tasks per the gem-owned naming convention
  • --debug and --verbose built-in class_option declarations on Tasks — set $DEBUG/$VERBOSE before any task runs via the invoke_command hook in Asgard::Base
  • debug? and verbose? private predicate helpers on Tasks — thin wrappers around $DEBUG and $VERBOSE for use inside task bodies
  • _ prefix convention for gem-owned methods in Tasks — built-in methods use _ prefix to distinguish them from user-defined tasks
  • run! guards against direct invocation of _-prefixed commands with a clean error message and exit 1
  • examples/ directory with working .loki files:
  • kitchen_sink.loki — demonstrates the full Thor DSL (all option types, long_desc, class_option, default_task, map, depends_on, var, no_commands, private)
  • server_subcommands.loki — subcommand group for server management
  • db_subcommands.loki — subcommand group for database management with depends_on chaining
  • README sections: Helper methods, Subcommands, Thor wrapper callout

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Replaced warn/exit 1 with abort throughout run! — Kernel#warn is silenced when $VERBOSE = nil, which is the default in Ruby 4.0; abort writes to $stderr regardless

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• --debug and --verbose promoted from mapped tasks to class_option — they now work as modifiers alongside other commands (e.g. asgard build --debug) rather than as standalone commands
  • Removed all references to just task runner and recipe terminology; Asgard uses "task" throughout
  • depends_on parameter renamed from *recipes to *tasks for consistency

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Parallel dependency execution — wrap deps in an array to run them concurrently: depends_on [:build, :lint] or depends_on :setup, [:build, :lint], :deploy
  • Asgard.run!(argv) — single entry point encapsulating find, load, validate, and start
  • Asgard.load_loki(dir) — auto-loads all *.loki files in a directory alphabetically
  • Tasks class pre-defined by the gem (class Tasks < Asgard::Base) — task files reopen it without restating the superclass
  • lib/asgard/tasks.rb — ships the pre-defined Tasks class

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Replaced SimpleFlow dependency with Dagwood — purpose-built DAG library with no extra dependencies and no Ruby 4 compatibility issues
  • bin/asgard simplified to two lines: require "asgard" + Asgard.run!(ARGV)
  • Task file convention: .loki is the project root marker and entry point; *.loki files each reopen class Tasks and are auto-loaded before .loki
  • Asgard.find_task_files renamed to Asgard.find_task_file (singular — only .loki is the entry point)
  • depends_on now accepts mixed sequential/parallel stages; bare symbols run sequentially, arrays within the splat run in parallel
  • run! handles its own errors — missing .loki and circular dependencies produce a clean one-line message and exit 1 rather than a backtrace
  • Thread-safe dep deduplication via class-level _ran_tasks Set + Mutex replaces Thor's @_invocations
  • Removed import macro — task files use Ruby class reopening instead of modules

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• SimpleFlow dependency (replaced by Dagwood)
  • logger gem workaround (was only needed for SimpleFlow on Ruby 4)
  • *.loki glob fallback in find_task_file — only .loki is the auto-discovered entry point

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Asgard::Base — Thor subclass providing the task DSL
  • depends_on — declare task dependencies; dependencies run at most once per invocation
  • var — declare static or lazy-evaluated variables available to all tasks
  • import — flat-merge a task module into the current class
  • dotenv — load a .env file into the environment
  • sh — run a shell command or multiline heredoc script; exits with the command's status on failure
  • shebang — write a script body to a tempfile and execute it with a given interpreter (:python3, :node, :ruby, :perl, :bash, :sh, or any custom interpreter)
  • Asgard.find_task_files — search current directory and ancestors for task files
  • Task file resolution: .loki takes priority; falls back to all *.loki files sorted alphabetically
  • asgard executable — finds task files, validates dependency graph, dispatches via Thor
  • Circular dependency detection via SimpleFlow::DependencyGraph at startup
  • 100% test coverage enforced via SimpleCov (95% minimum threshold)
  • Quality task in .loki runs flog after tests

docs.title: Command Reference
docs.text: Everything you can type after asgard, on one page. The first section covers running your own tasks; the three after it cover the built-in commands schedule, watcher and jobs. Each table row is one line; the guide pages linked from each section go deeper.

docs.title: Running Tasks
docs.text:
asgard TASK [ARGUMENTS] [--option VALUE ...] [--debug] [--verbose]

Asgard looks for a .loki file in the current directory, then in each parent directory, and loads the first one it finds. Without one it stops: asgard: no .loki file found in /path. The three list commands below and bare asgard jobs are the exceptions; they work anywhere and then cover every project on the machine.

Command What it does asgard Runs the default_task if the project set one, otherwise shows help asgard TASK Runs TASK, its dependencies first asgard TASK ARG... Passes positional arguments to the task's method parameters asgard TASK --opt VALUE Sets an option declared with option or class_option asgard help Lists every task with its description, plus the project's header and footer asgard help TASK Usage, options and long_desc for one task asgard tree The tasks as a tree, subcommands expanded asgard --version Prints the version and exits; works without a .loki asgard --doctor Prints the diagnostic report and exits; works even when the .loki is broken asgard TASK --debug Runs the task with debug? true asgard TASK --verbose Runs the task with verbose? true; an import inside the task prints what it loads

--version and --doctor are asgard's own only before the task name. After it they belong to the task: asgard mytask --version hands --version to mytask.

docs.title: Prefix Matching and Aliases
docs.text:
Any unambiguous prefix of a task name runs it. An exact name always wins over a longer name it is a prefix of. An ambiguous prefix stops with a list of candidates.

asgard ru          # runs rubocop_check if it is the only task starting with "ru"
asgard test        # runs test, even though test_check also exists
asgard dep         # Ambiguous command dep matches [deploy, deploy_staging]

A map "t" => "test" in the .loki adds a name that stays stable whatever tasks are added later. See Defining Tasks.

docs.title: Built-in Flags
docs.text:
Flag Effect --debug debug? is true inside tasks; with --verbose, an import inside the task also reports files it skips --verbose verbose? is true inside tasks; an import inside the task prints each file it loads --version Print the version and exit --doctor Print the diagnostic report and exit

See Options & Flags and Help & Diagnostics.

docs.title: asgard schedule
docs.text:
Manages the entries declared with schedule :task, ... in the .loki. The scheduler is launchd on macOS and systemd user timers on Linux. Guide: Scheduled Tasks.

Command Arguments and flags What it does asgard schedule preview Prints the job files install would write, without writing them asgard schedule install Installs every declared entry and removes this project's entries that are no longer declared; prints installed NAME: asgard task args (17:30 weekdays) per entry asgard schedule list --all, -a A table of this project's installed entries (NAME, COMMAND, SCHEDULE, STATE, LAST EXIT); --all covers every project, grouped by Project: slug (/path) asgard schedule stop NAME Stops one entry; it stays stopped across reboots and reinstalls until started asgard schedule start NAME Starts a stopped entry, or installs and starts just this one declared entry asgard schedule trigger NAME Runs an installed entry now, under the scheduler; refused while the entry is stopped asgard schedule log NAME --follow, -f Prints the entry's log; -f keeps printing as output arrives asgard schedule remove [NAME] Removes one installed entry, or every entry of this project asgard schedule prune --dry-run, -n Removes every project's entries whose project directory no longer exists; -n only lists them

STATE is active, running, stopped or not loaded. LAST EXIT is the exit code, never run, or - for a stopped entry.

Naming another project's entry. stop, start, trigger, log and remove accept project/NAME, where project is the slug shown by list --all or just the project's directory name when that is enough to pick it out. A bare NAME means this project's entry first, then any other project's; when two other projects share the name, asgard asks you to write project/NAME.

Run install again after changing a declaration or your PATH.

docs.title: asgard watcher
docs.text:
Runs and manages the file watcher for the entries declared with watch :task, paths: .... One watcher process per project. Guide: Watched Files.

Command Arguments and flags What it does asgard watcher start Starts the watcher in the background; prints started watcher for <slug> (pid N); log: <path>; refused if one is running asgard watcher stop Stops the watcher; a task already running finishes first, and stop names it while it waits asgard watcher list --all, -a A table of this project's watches (NAME, TASK, WATCHES, DAEMON, LAST RUN); --all covers every project asgard watcher preview Prints the exact command and environment each entry would run asgard watcher log --follow, -f Prints the watcher's log; -f keeps following it asgard watcher run Watches in the foreground until Ctrl-C or TERM; this is what start runs detached

DAEMON is running or stopped. LAST RUN is never, running (pid N), did not finish (pid N), or the exit status with duration and time, such as 0 (0.4s, 2026-10-18 23:40:02).

Saving a loaded .loki file while the watcher runs restarts it with the new declarations.

docs.title: asgard jobs
docs.text:
Lists, stops and restarts the background jobs started with sh "...", background: true (or background: :name). Guide: Background Jobs.

Command Arguments and flags What it does asgard jobs Same as list asgard jobs list --all, -a A table of this project's jobs (JOB, TASK, PID, STATUS, STARTED, COMMAND); --all covers every project asgard jobs stop [NAME...], --all / -a, --timeout N / -t N Stops jobs by job name, or by task name (including jobs its dependencies started); no name stops every job of this project; --all stops every project's; TERM first, KILL after N seconds (default 10) asgard jobs log NAME --follow, -f Prints the job's log (stdout and stderr of its latest run); -f follows it asgard jobs restart NAME --timeout N / -t N Stops the job, then runs its owning task again, dependencies included asgard jobs clean Forgets every job that is no longer running: record, script, status and log

STATUS is running, exited N (2.5s) or gone (the process is not there and no exit status was recorded, as after a reboot).

stop prints one line per job: stopped api (pid 48213), killed db-1 (pid 48201) after 10s, or doc_server-1 is not running. It exits 1 when any job had to be killed or any name matched nothing. stop --all takes no names.

docs.title: Working Outside a Project
docs.text:
These commands do not need a .loki above the current directory. Run from anywhere, they cover every project on the machine:

asgard schedule list
asgard watcher list
asgard jobs list
asgard jobs

Every other command needs a project, because it reads the project's .loki to know its tasks and declarations.

docs.title: Exit Status
docs.text:
Condition Status Task finished normally 0 Task returned :fail 1 A sh or shebang script failed the script's exit status A script was ended by a signal 128 + the signal number Shell or interpreter not found 127 abort or raise Asgard::Error in a task 1 Usage error: missing argument, unknown task, unknown option 1 No .loki found, a .loki failed to load, or a dependency graph is invalid 1 asgard jobs stop had to kill a job, or a name matched nothing 1 Ctrl-C 130

Details and the messages that go with each case are in Help & Diagnostics.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
depends_on says what must run before a task. You list the prerequisites above the task, and asgard runs them in order, runs groups of them at the same time where you ask for that, and makes sure each one runs only once no matter how many tasks need it. Dependencies are what turn a pile of commands into a pipeline.

The simplest form is one task that needs another:

class Tasks
  desc "Compile the project"
  def build = sh "rake build"

  depends_on :build
  desc "Run the test suite"
  def test = sh "rake test"
end

asgard test    # runs build, then test

Note

desc and depends_on both go above the def, in either order. depends_on always attaches to the very next method.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
When you run asgard <task>:

  1. Every .loki file loads and every dependency list is checked: unknown task names, cycles and a few other mistakes stop asgard before anything runs (see Startup Validation).
  2. The task's prerequisites run stage by stage. A stage is one task, or a group of tasks that run at the same time. The next stage starts when every task in the current one has finished.
  3. The task itself runs.

Each task runs at most once per asgard command, however many other tasks depend on it. A prerequisite that fails stops the whole run with a non-zero exit status.

docs.title: Sequential Dependencies
docs.text:
Bare task names run one after another, left to right:

class Tasks
  desc "Compile the project"
  def build = sh "rake build"

  depends_on :build
  desc "Run the test suite"
  def test = sh "rake test"

  depends_on :test
  desc "Publish the gem"
  def release = sh "bundle exec rake release"
end

asgard release   # build → test → release

Several names in one depends_on also run in order:

depends_on :clean, :build, :test
desc "Clean, build, and test"
def package = sh "rake package"

asgard package   # clean → build → test → package

docs.title: Parallel Dependencies
docs.text:
Wrap names in an array and they run at the same time. Asgard waits for the whole group before moving on:

class Tasks
  desc "Check code style"
  def lint = sh "bundle exec rubocop"

  desc "Run type checks"
  def typecheck = sh "bundle exec srb tc"

  depends_on [:lint, :typecheck]
  desc "Run tests (after lint and typecheck)"
  def test = sh "bundle exec rake test"
end

asgard test   # lint ∥ typecheck → test

Parallel tasks run in threads inside one asgard process. For shell commands and other work that waits on the outside world, that is real concurrency: two sh calls in two parallel tasks are two processes running at once. The output of parallel tasks interleaves on the terminal; examples/concurrent.loki in the repository shows this on purpose.

docs.title: Mixed Sequential and Parallel
docs.text:
Mix bare names and arrays in one depends_on. Each element is a stage:

class Tasks
  desc "Install dependencies"; def setup  = sh "bundle install"
  desc "Check code style";     def lint   = sh "bundle exec rubocop"
  desc "Compile assets";       def build  = sh "rake assets:precompile"
  desc "Run tests";            def test   = sh "bundle exec rake test"
  desc "Post to Slack";        def notify = sh "curl $SLACK_WEBHOOK -d '{\"text\":\"done\"}'"

  # setup first, then lint and build together, then test, then notify
  depends_on :setup, [:lint, :build], :test, :notify
  desc "Full CI pipeline"
  def ci = puts "CI complete"
end

asgard ci
